title: The Spiritual Armament
english: He slackens the hands of warriors, and a negligent monk enfeebles the zeal of the brothers. A swarm of bees produces the honeycomb, and a fellowship of brothers the kingdom of heaven. A trumpet rouses the zeal of warriors, and the teaching of practical virtue [rouses] the diligence of disciples.

Arm your brothers with words, O leader — †of fingers† — and breastplate them with the promises of the coming good things; fence them with the shield of faith through their contests, and greave them with hope toward God. Stir the feet in the lessons of the gospel, and gird the loins with the words of temperance; put a sword into the hand, and the sharpest anger against the passions, and draw up a phalanx in opposition against the pleasure of the passions. Train in the thoughts the soldiers who are experienced for battle, and show them fearsome.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG De magistris et discipulis u01-rem-early

title: The Teacher as Physician
english: …the defeat, by the threat of eternal punishment. Proclaim the victor with splendid praises, for even praise knows how to make men more diligent; and heal the one who has been injured, with sympathy — for forgiveness turns back the prudent man no less than a threat. Let him not be moved with anger against a disciple who has sinned, for it is not holy to wound oneself before healing another; but correct him toward the good without malice. For a doctor heals the passion but feels no indignation against one who fell ill involuntarily. A doctor, while cutting, does this without anger; and a teacher, while rebuking, let him not mix anger with the rebuke. Guide those fleeing to the land of Egypt through the desert by a way; for he knows that…

title: The Path to Virtue
english: It is a small thing to train toward self-control those who are beginning in virtue. Pitch your tent at Elim — and the gates themselves are interpreted as a symbol of the entrance that leads to virtue — and show the seventy palm trees. Encamp by the twelve springs — for the palm trees must also sing back to you of victory, as a symbol, and the springs richly furnish waters to quench the flame of the passions — until, having cast down all the foreign nations, they reach the land of promise, in which they will live the blessed life of dispassion, receiving true joy as the reward of their labors.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
